profile.name: Kelina Cyril
profile.title: PhD Student, Cellular & Molecular Neurobiology
profile.tagline: Driven by curiosity about the microscopic architecture of the mind.
bio: I explore how living neurons communicate, adapt, and build the foundation of our memories. Combining an early love for biological photography with advanced microscopy, I spend my days peering into the quiet, complex beauty of cellular networks.
For me, science is both rigorous biophysics and deep creative wonder—tracing how thought and memory physically emerge at the nanometer scale.

blogs.title: Resolving Nanometer-Scale Actin Dynamics in Dendritic Spines with STED
blogs.excerpt: How stimulated emission depletion nanoscopy bypasses the classical Abbe diffraction barrier to track rapid spine neck contractility following theta-burst induction.
blogs.content:
### The Diffraction Challenge in Live Synapses

For over a century, light microscopy was bound by Ernst Abbe's diffraction limit: structures closer together than approximately half the wavelength of light (~200 nm) blur into a single diffraction spot. In synaptic biology, this was catastrophic. Dendritic spine necks often narrow to 50–100 nm, and the postsynaptic density (PSD) measures under 350 nm across.

Stimulated Emission Depletion (STED) nanoscopy breaks this barrier by pairing an excitation laser beam with a donut-shaped depletion laser beam that turns off fluorophores at the periphery via stimulated emission, leaving only a sub-diffraction focal spot in the center.

### Overcoming Phototoxicity in Living Slices

When imaging organotypic hippocampal slices, excessive STED beam power causes immediate photobleaching and local heating artifacts. In our protocol:

1. **Gating Time Windows**: Using time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC) allows us to reject early scattered photons and reduce required continuous depletion beam intensities by 40%.
2. **Fluorophore Pairing**: We paired silicon rhodamine (SiR-Actin) with STAR 580 to minimize spectral bleed-through while ensuring rapid cell permeability without aggressive electroporation.
3. **Perfusion Stability**: Constant oxygenated artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF) with 95% O₂ / 5% CO₂ maintained at 32°C prevents focal drift.

> *"Resolving the spine neck in real time transformed our understanding of compartmentalized biochemical signaling from a theoretical model into an observable physical event."*

### Key Takeaways
- Spines exhibit rapid neck twitch contractions within 180 seconds of local glutamate uncaging.
- Actin ring periodicities (~190 nm along dendritic shafts) stabilize within mature spine necks, acting as structural girders during long-term potentiation.

blogs.title: In Vivo Two-Photon Calcium Imaging: Navigating Artifacts in Cortical Layer 2/3
blogs.excerpt: Practical techniques for mitigating brain motion, neuropil contamination, and z-drift during awake-behaving mouse visual cortex assays.
blogs.content:
### Recording Cellular Ensembles in Awake Animals

Investigating neural plasticity during learning requires monitoring identified ensembles of pyramidal neurons across multiple consecutive days. In Layer 2/3 of mouse primary visual cortex, GCaMP8s enables single-action-potential resolution. However, awake imaging introduces challenges that do not exist in slice preparations.

### Handling Neuropil Spillover and Z-Drift

The dense intertwining of unmyelinated axons and dendrites produces a diffuse background fluorescence (neuropil signal) that contaminates somatic regions of interest (ROIs).

```python
# Neuropil subtraction formula
# F_corrected(t) = F_soma(t) - r * F_neuropil(t)
# where r is empirically calibrated between 0.65 and 0.75
```

### Surgical Cranial Window Optimization

- **3mm Double-Coverglass Technique**: A 3mm round glass coverslip glued to a 4mm outer ring creates gentle subdural pressure, virtually eliminating respiration-induced brain pulsations.
- **Titanium Headplates**: Precision CNC-milled titanium headplates secured with cyanoacrylate and dental cement guarantee zero mechanical flex during head-fixation on the spherical treadmill.

> *"Signal fidelity in calcium imaging is 80% preparation mechanics and 20% post-processing algorithms. A pristine optical window always outperforms the most sophisticated deconvolution filter."*

blogs.title: Connectomics at the Crossroads: Deep Learning in Synaptic Vesicle Segmentation
blogs.excerpt: How hybrid 3D U-Nets and boundary distance transforms accelerate volumetric reconstruction of presynaptic active zones by 100x.
blogs.content:
### The Manual Annotation Bottleneck

High-pressure freezing followed by cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) produces unprecedented three-dimensional volumes of intact synaptic boutons. Yet, segmenting individual neurotransmitter vesicles (each ~40 nm in diameter) and tracing active zone membranes manually took weeks per cubic micrometer.

### Architecture of Our Segmentation Pipeline

We deployed a customized 3D Residual U-Net with isotropic voxel resampling and deep spatial feature extraction:

1. **Sphere Distance Transform**: Predicting center coordinates rather than binary masks prevents touching vesicle instances from fusing into amorphous blobs.
2. **Postsynaptic Density (PSD) Tracing**: Integrating multi-scale attention heads allowed automated recognition of electron-dense PSD matrices without manual seed point placement.

### Experimental Verification

Benchmarked against manual ground truth annotated by three independent neurobiologists, the automated segmentation achieved a 96.4% F1-score across 14,000 vesicles while slashing annotation time from 42 hours to 18 minutes.
